title: auth.Service is 20 methods across six unrelated concerns, and every consumer that needs two of them hand-rolls a 20-method fake

evidence.claim: auth.Service declares 20 methods, grouped by its own comments into six concerns: OAuth flow, session management, user management, token storage, email allowlist, admin.
evidence.command: git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/domain/auth/service.go | awk '/^type Service interface \{/,/^\}/' | grep -cE '^\t[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\('

evidence.claim: Three separate test packages each declare their own inline mockAuthService implementing all 20 methods. This also breaches CLAUDE.md's stated rule 'Mocks: Import from internal/testutil/mocks/ - never create inline mocks'; internal/testutil/mocks/ has no auth.Service mock (only auth_repository.go and auth_inmemory.go, which mock auth.Repository).

The scheduler consumer calls exactly 2 of the 20 methods, yet its test must stub all 20. This is the concrete cost: 18 no-op stub methods written three times over to exercise 2, 2 and 4 real methods respectively.

The middleware consumer calls 2 of 20 (GetOrCreateUser, ValidateSession) and the admin handler calls 4 of 20 (AddAllowedEmail, ListAllowedEmails, ListUsers, RemoveAllowedEmail) — no consumer in the repo uses the interface as a whole.
evidence.output:
h.authService.AddAllowedEmail
h.authService.ListAllowedEmails
h.authService.ListUsers
h.authService.RemoveAllowedEmail
m.authService.GetOrCreateUser
m.authService.ValidateSession

evidence.claim: Two production types must implement all 20 methods, so adding a seventh concern to the interface costs 2 production implementations plus 3 test fakes.

searched_universe: All Go interface declarations in non-test, non-testutil files under internal/ and cmd/ at the pinned revision, enumerated via `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev>` filtered to '*.go', with per-interface method counts computed by an awk scan of top-level `type X interface {` blocks. auth.Service (20) and inventory.PurchaseDHRepository (20) were the two widest; the latter is explicitly excluded per CLAUDE.md's statement that the inventory repository split is by concern and intentional, and it carries no equivalent inline-mock cost (internal/testutil/mocks/ provides shared mocks for it).
exclusions: *_test.go files excluded from the interface-width scan itself (test-local interfaces are not a production seam), though test files were searched for implementations
internal/testutil/** excluded from the width scan for the same reason
inventory repository interfaces deliberately not filed: CLAUDE.md states the split is by concern and that PurchaseRepository's size is intentional, and no concrete cost was found
proposed_fix: Leave auth.Service as the composite the composition root wires, but declare narrow consumer-side interfaces at each point of use, as the repo already does elsewhere (e.g. dhpricing.NewService takes PurchaseLookup / DHPriceUpdater / DHPriceWriter seams rather than one wide store). Concretely: a 2-method SessionJanitor for scheduler/session_cleanup.go, a 2-method SessionValidator for middleware/auth.go, and a 4-method AdminDirectory for handlers/admin.go. Each test then fakes 2-4 methods instead of 20, and the three inline mockAuthService declarations collapse. Alternatively, if a shared fake is preferred, add one auth.Service mock to internal/testutil/mocks/ per the stated convention — that removes the duplication but not the width.
acceptance_criteria: `go build ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass after the change.
`git grep -c 'func (m \*mockAuthService)' -- '*_test.go'` returns either no matches or counts of 4 or fewer per file, proving no test still stubs 20 methods to exercise 2.
`var _ auth.Service = (*google.OAuthService)(nil)` still compiles, proving the composite interface was not silently narrowed out from under its production implementations.
`make check` passes (lint + import check + file size + Playwright version).

title: The size check exempts cmd/slabledger/main.go by name with no ceiling and no stated reason, and that file holds the largest function in the repository

evidence.claim: scripts/check-file-size.sh excludes cmd/slabledger/main.go by exact path. The script comments the *_test.go exclusion ('table-driven tests grow naturally') but gives no reason for the main.go or testutil exclusions.
The exemption is effective: main.go is absent from the set the check iterates, so no line count of any size would ever produce a WARN or FAIL for it.
evidence.command: mkdir -p /tmp/sizecheck && git archive 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6 | tar -x -C /tmp/sizecheck && cd /tmp/sizecheck && find internal/ cmd/ -name '*.go' ! -name '*_test.go' ! -path '*/testutil/*' ! -path 'cmd/slabledger/main.go' -type f | grep -c '^cmd/slabledger/main.go$'

evidence.claim: runServer occupies lines 150-418 of main.go — 269 lines, the single largest function in all non-test, non-testutil Go under internal/ and cmd/, and 64% of the exempted file.
evidence.command: git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:cmd/slabledger/main.go | awk 'NR>=150 && /^}$/{print "runServer: lines 150-" NR " = " NR-150+1 " lines"; exit}'

evidence.claim: The exemption is a single-file special case, not a directory policy: main.go's siblings in the same package (handlers.go, init_schedulers.go, init_inventory_services.go, server.go) are all inside the checked set and subject to the 500/600 budget.
evidence.output:
cmd/slabledger/adapters.go
cmd/slabledger/admin.go
cmd/slabledger/dh_card_id_resolver.go
cmd/slabledger/handlers.go
cmd/slabledger/init_inventory_services.go
cmd/slabledger/init_schedulers.go
cmd/slabledger/init_services.go
cmd/slabledger/main.go
cmd/slabledger/server.go
cmd/slabledger/shutdown.go — of these ten, only main.go is exempted

searched_universe: scripts/check-file-size.sh at the pinned revision, plus every non-test, non-testutil '*.go' file under internal/ and cmd/ enumerated from `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev>`, with line counts from `git show <rev>:<path> | wc -l` and top-level function extents from an awk scan for `^func ` .. `^}`.
exclusions: web/ — the size check does not cover it at all; that gap belongs to the frontend-health lens, noted here only as scope, not claimed as this finding
*_test.go and internal/testutil/** — checked and found to contain no non-mock production logic, so those two exclusions are behaving as intended (internal/testutil holds only config.go plus mocks/)
proposed_fix: Replace the unconditional `! -path 'cmd/slabledger/main.go'` exemption with either (a) no exemption — main.go is 418 lines at this baseline and passes the 500 guideline today, so removing the special case costs nothing and restores the ceiling; or (b) if the exemption is deliberate, a comment stating why, matching the style of the *_test.go comment two lines above. Separately, extracting runServer's distinct phases (metrics server setup, auth wiring, DH wiring, scheduler deps assembly) into named helpers alongside the existing initializeCampaignsService / initializeSchedulers / createHandlers would bring the largest function in the repo in line with the composition-root helpers it already calls.
acceptance_criteria: `bash scripts/check-file-size.sh` exits 0 with the exemption removed, proving main.go is under the 600 hard limit without the special case.
If runServer is also split: `go build ./cmd/slabledger` succeeds and `./slabledger --help` still prints usage, proving startup wiring was not reordered.

title: core_types.go emerged from the SLA-32 file split already at 562 lines — 38 from the CI hard fail — on the one file every inventory feature must touch

evidence.claim: core_types.go is 562 lines, the largest non-excluded source file in the repo and the closest to the 600-line hard fail. It is one of six files in the WARN band; there are zero FAILs at baseline.
evidence.command: mkdir -p /tmp/sizecheck && git archive 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6 | tar -x -C /tmp/sizecheck && cd /tmp/sizecheck && bash scripts/check-file-size.sh
evidence.output:
WARN: internal/domain/portfolio/service.go (540 lines, guideline 500)
WARN: internal/domain/inventory/core_types.go (562 lines, guideline 500)
WARN: internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/campaigns_psa.go (518 lines, guideline 500)
WARN: internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/campaigns_purchases.go (520 lines, guideline 500)
WARN: internal/adapters/scheduler/dh_analytics_refresh_steps.go (542 lines, guideline 500)
WARN: internal/adapters/scheduler/cardladder_refresh.go (525 lines, guideline 500)

File size check passed with warnings.

evidence.claim: The file was created two days before this baseline by commit c624b9a7, a refactor whose stated purpose was to split inventory files by contents (SLA-32) — and it landed at 562 lines, already in the WARN band. The split axis that produced it is therefore already spent: this file is the residue after the obvious extractions were made.
evidence.command: git log -1 --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short c624b9a7 && git show c624b9a7:internal/domain/inventory/core_types.go | wc -l
evidence.output:
c624b9a7 2026-08-08 refactor(inventory): rename mis-named files and split by actual contents (SLA-32) (#586)
562

evidence.claim: The file holds the hub's shared persisted types — Campaign, Purchase, Sale, and 18 more type declarations — so almost any inventory feature that persists a new field must edit it. Purchase alone spans 100 lines (274-373).

The maintenance cost is a CI failure landing on an unrelated author: 38 lines of headroom is roughly one feature that adds a handful of fields to Campaign plus Purchase plus Sale. Whoever's PR crosses 600 must split the hub's core type file as an unplanned prerequisite, and the check hard-fails rather than warning.

searched_universe: Every non-test, non-testutil '*.go' file under internal/ and cmd/ at the pinned revision, enumerated from `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev>` and line-counted with `git show <rev>:<path> | wc -l`, cross-checked by running the project's own scripts/check-file-size.sh against a `git archive` extraction of the pinned tree.
exclusions: *_test.go, internal/testutil/**, and cmd/slabledger/main.go — the size check's own exclusion set; the main.go exemption is filed separately as SIZE-002
web/ — not covered by the Go size check
proposed_fix: Split core_types.go along the aggregate boundary the file already exhibits: move Sale, BulkSaleInput, BulkSaleResult and BulkSaleError (lines 465-536) into a sale_types.go, and the activation/revocation group (ActivationCheck, ActivationChecklist, RevocationFlag, lines 537-562) into campaign_activation_types.go. Both are pure type moves within the same package, so no import changes anywhere. That leaves core_types.go around 460 lines, back under the 500 guideline with real headroom, without disturbing Campaign/Purchase — the two types with the most call sites.
acceptance_criteria: `bash scripts/check-file-size.sh` no longer lists internal/domain/inventory/core_types.go in its WARN output.
`go build ./...` and `go test -race ./internal/domain/inventory/...` pass — a pure intra-package type move must not change any import or any behavior.
`git diff --stat` shows only additions and deletions of type declarations, with no edits to any type body, confirming the change is a move rather than a rewrite.

title: The two largest domain functions each sit in a file just under the 500-line warn line, so the enforced size budget reports nothing about them

evidence.claim: ImportCerts spans lines 63-296 of service_cert_entry.go — 234 lines, 48% of a 491-line file. The file is 9 lines below the 500-line WARN threshold, so `make check` is silent about it.
evidence.command: git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/domain/inventory/service_cert_entry.go | wc -l && git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/domain/inventory/service_cert_entry.go | awk 'NR>=63 && /^}$/{print "ImportCerts: 63-" NR " = " NR-63+1 " lines"; exit}'

evidence.claim: The same shape repeats one package over: ImportPSAExportGlobal is 239 lines inside a 498-line file — two lines under the warn line. The two largest domain functions in the repo are both hidden by a metric measured per file rather than per function.
evidence.command: git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/domain/csvimport/service_import_psa.go | wc -l && git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/domain/csvimport/service_import_psa.go | awk 'NR>=26 && /^}$/{print "ImportPSAExportGlobal: 26-" NR " = " NR-26+1 " lines"; exit}'

evidence.claim: ImportCerts is not merely long: it carries 29 control-flow branches, 14 early exits from a single loop body, and 6 levels of indentation, all mutating one shared `result` accumulator. Its responsibilities are input dedup, campaign bootstrap, two batch lookups, sold-item detection, export-flag and received-at writes, DH push enrollment, circuit-breaker latching, PSA category/name normalization, purchase construction, duplicate-cert recovery, two enrichment queues, and a background goroutine — thirteen concerns in one function body.

The maintenance cost is measurable in the test suite: exercising this one function requires service_cert_entry_test.go, the largest test file in the repository at 1288 lines, which names ImportCerts 38 times. Every new branch inside the function multiplies against the setup those tests already carry.
1288 lines is the maximum across every *_test.go in the repo, so this is the worst case rather than a typical one.

searched_universe: Top-level function extents across every non-test, non-testutil '*.go' file under internal/ and cmd/ at the pinned revision, computed by an awk scan for `^func ` through the next `^}` over a `git archive` extraction of the pinned tree, sorted by length. The five longest are runServer (269, filed as SIZE-002), createHandlers (264), ImportPSAExportGlobal (239), ImportCerts (234) and CardLadderRefreshScheduler.runOnce (225).
exclusions: *_test.go and internal/testutil/** excluded from the function-length scan (table-driven test bodies are long by design); test files were still searched for the cost evidence above

createHandlers (264 lines, cmd/slabledger/handlers.go) deliberately not filed — it is straight-line dependency wiring in the composition root with no branching, which is a different and much lower hazard than a branching import loop
The awk extent scan assumes gofmt output (top-level closing brace at column 0); the repo is gofmt-clean under `make check`, but a hand-formatted function would be missed
proposed_fix: Extract the two arms of ImportCerts' loop body into named methods on the service: `handleExistingCert(ctx, existing, certNum, now, salesMap, result)` for the already-in-inventory branch (lines 108-157) and `importNewCert(ctx, certNum, now, result) (imported bool)` for the lookup-and-create branch (lines 159-281), leaving ImportCerts as dedup, batch lookups, loop, and the background resolver kick-off — roughly 60 lines. This is the same decomposition csvimport already applies elsewhere (handleExistingPSAPurchase is a named method extracted from the import path). Apply the equivalent split to ImportPSAExportGlobal. Separately, consider whether the size budget should measure functions as well as files — the current per-file metric is what allowed both of these to grow unremarked.
acceptance_criteria: `go test -race ./internal/domain/inventory/... ./internal/domain/csvimport/...` passes with no changes to the existing test assertions — the extraction must be behavior-preserving, and the 1288-line test file is the proof harness.
An awk scan for top-level function extents over the changed files shows no function above 120 lines.

The circuit-breaker latch is still batch-wide after the split: a test where the first cert lookup returns ErrCodeProviderCircuitOpen must still mark every remaining cert Retryable without issuing further lookups (the psaUnavailable flag must be threaded, not duplicated per-call).
